speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Access to these loans is deliberately made easy to help as many students as possible.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, this was never meant to be a commercial operation, but part of our policy to help students with their education and it also serves a social objective.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The loans are interest-free during the period of study.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These loan repayment terms represent an intended subsidy from the Government.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They are made flexible to give students time to settle down in their careers and to lessen their financial burden immediately upon graduation.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As students earn more over time, they may then adjust the monthly repayment upwards to pay off their loans as quickly as possible.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Notwithstanding, we expect students to be responsible in repaying their loans.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For borrowers who are late in making their loan repayments, there are established processes in place for the banks to follow up with them.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The banks will first send reminder letters and make follow-up phone calls.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If the delay becomes severe, Letters of Demand may then be sent to the borrower, and the guarantor for the loan alerted, and legal processes can start.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Auditor-General's Office (AGO) has made certain observations on the operation of the student loan schemes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There is an observation on the review of agency fees payable to the banks.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The review really should not have taken so long.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We are already in talks with the institutions and banks and will get the review done as soon as possible.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will also need to enforce the processes to manage loan recovery more promptly.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As the Member pointed out, while doing so, there will be cases where we need to exercise some flexibility, especially when the borrowers require more time or face temporary difficulties in repaying their loans on time.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is in line with the spirit and policy intent of the student loan schemes.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The main reasons today for appeals received by MOE from such borrowers are: (a) they were pursuing further studies and did not have income to pay off the loans; (b) they are still unemployed or seeking employment; and (c) medical or family reasons, such as the borrower or his family members falling seriously ill.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOE assesses each of these appeals individually, taking into account their unique circumstances.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Many have been granted temporary deferment of payments.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The students who were offered deferment do repay their loans over time.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And write-off of loans is considered only as a last resort when the banks have exhausted all means and all efforts to recover them.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: MOE intends to continue to exercise sensitivity, judgement and compassion in dealing with these cases, to help our students.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: AGO has advised MOE to incentivise the banks to ensure more expedient loan recoveries.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think that should be reviewed and we are already doing so.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There are various ways to tweak the formula and we will need to strike a balance.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But more importantly, if need be, we will have to articulate the social objective and the purpose of student loans more clearly, so as to facilitate future auditors' work in this area.
